svg.title: Fig. 204 — Mercator's map of a great-circle route: sphere, cylinder, plane and rays
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 204, page 230. Section: trigonometric.

g.data-text: The earth as a sphere of radius R, with the centre G (the point from which the map is projected).
The cylinder that circumscribes the sphere along the equator, its axis the N–S line: two vertical walls tangent to the sphere, with the front edges of its top and bottom rims.

The plane of the great-circle route, through the centre G (drawn as a parallelogram), and its section with the sphere: the route, an ellipse in this view, seen in full on the near side and dashed behind.
Rays from G through points of the route (dashed) meet the wall of the cylinder: the points where they land are the Mercator map of the route on the cylinder.

Cut the cylinder along an element and lay it flat (right): the route becomes one period of a sine curve, whose height above the equator is proportional to the tangent of the latitude (hence to sin of the longitude measured from the node).
g.text: one period of a sine curve
